If discriminant is positive, you'll get two real solutions. If zero, one real solution. If negative, two complex solutions. Use the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / 2a. Plug in your numbers, calculate both plus and minus versions. Check your solutions by substituting back into original equation.

First, find the derivative f'(x) of your function. Stationary points occur where f'(x) = 0, so set the derivative equal to zero and solve for x. These x-values are potential stationary points.
